author: @fl0rianr

evidence.api_compatibility: LemonadeAPI.systemInfo() gained an optional { afterPending?, maxAgeMs? } parameter with sensible defaults, so existing callers are unaffected. The new onSystemInfoChange() method is additive. _refreshBackendStatusAfterLoad() changed its signature to accept a recipe string and options object, but it is private and called only from loadModel() within the same file, which was updated accordingly. No breaking change.
evidence.documentation: This is a bug fix for existing GUI behavior; no API spec, guide, or behavior-documentation update was needed or provided.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The commit changes the GUI on the Models page (backend readiness badge) and the Backends page (install triggers). No human non-test harness exercised the Models page with a backend update scenario. A tester should verify the badge syncs as described in the maintainer to-dos.
evidence.post_approval_commits: One commit (28943c0, by @fl0rianr) was pushed after @meghsat's sole approval at 01:01:11Z. It tightened the load-trigger refresh to only fire when the selected backend is not already installed, made the focus-refresh scope cover all stale backend states, and updated tests. The scope remained within the PR's stated purpose and risk profile. No re-approval was sought.
evidence.review: PR #3977 was requested to @kpoineal (GUI, app, a11y) and @jeremyfowers (GUI design language). Neither left any human review comments. The only approval came from @meghsat, who co-authored the merge commit. The only human review activity was an automated bot (coderabbitai[bot]) that flagged four edge cases (stale responses after disconnect, request-ordering races, retry-on-failure, focus-refresh scope); the author addressed three and declined to add a retry scheduler, citing the tab-focus recovery path. Subject-area expertise was absent from the review.
evidence.security: The change subscribes to /api/v1/system-info and /api/v1/downloads responses and updates React state from them. It does not introduce credential handling, network calls to external endpoints, code execution, or permission broadening. The generation-based stale-response guard prevents cross-connection state leaks when the user switches servers. No security concern.
evidence.tests: New assertions were added to src/app/tests/model-state-deduplication.runtime.cjs: subscriber delivery across system-info snapshots, stale-request rejection via generation check, unsubscribe cleanup, maxAgeMs caching, pre-disconnect snapshot invalidation, /load-trigger refresh with backend-state awareness, and focus-refresh deduplication. The existing model-state-deduplication test was extended rather than weakened. Manual testing was reported by the author (npm run typecheck, npm run test:model-state, manual backend install → warning clears).

maintainer_todos.text: Open the Models page, click Load on a model, wait for it to start, then switch away and back: confirm the 'Engine update required' badge clears after the load completes without needing to press F5.
On the Backends page, install a backend for a model, return to the Models page and confirm the stale badge disappears immediately without F5.
Alt-Tab away from Lemonade then back: confirm only one /system-info request fires when no backend needs updating, and multiple requests fire when update_required backends are present.

shout_outs.reason: Co-authored the merge commit and submitted a substantive commit (4509cebe) that fixed three additional edge cases: backend updates triggered by /load not refreshing the badge, narrow focus-refresh scope, and redundant system-info requests on every window focus, along with tests.

subject: fix(gui): sync model backend warnings after backend updates (#3977)
summary: Adds an onSystemInfoChange subscriber to the Models page, subscribes ModelManager to completed backend downloads and window-focus events, and adds a generation-based stale-response guard to system-info calls — keeping the backend readiness badge in sync after backend updates without requiring F5.
verdict_reason: The two requested GUI reviewers (@kpoineal, @jeremyfowers) left no substantive review comments; only an automated bot review and a co-author approval were obtained, despite the commit introducing a complex multi-file state-management change.
